comparison: Perfect agreement on behavioral results (C21-C28). Both evaluations find the behavioral data supported with appropriate statistical tests demonstrating successful experimental manipulation.

Disagreement on interpretive claims about DMN organization (C79-C82). OpenEval finds these claims supported, while peer reviewers express uncertainty due to concerns about generalizability beyond scenes to other stimulus categories.

Agreement on gradient analysis findings (C62-C65). Both evaluations accept the gradient characterization showing semantic pathway as more abstract and spatial pathway as more anchored in visual processing.

Agreement on univariate integration findings (C66, C68-C69). Both evaluations support the angular gyrus activation patterns during semantic-spatial alignment, though OpenEval provides more detailed analysis including C67.
Partial overlap on connectivity patterns (C70-C71). Both evaluations accept these connectivity findings as part of the solid evidence base for integration regions.
Agreement on background claims about DMN (C1-C8). Both evaluations accept these established foundational claims from prior literature without question.
Agreement on DMN subdivision background (C9-C13). Both evaluations accept these established claims about DMN subsystems as supported by prior research.
Agreement on visual processing background (C14-C20). Both evaluations accept these established claims about visual pathways as supported foundational knowledge.

Agreement on core dual pathway findings (C73-C75). Both evaluations strongly support the main conclusion about dissociable pathways, with peer reviewers explicitly affirming 'clear evidence of stimulus-based processing dissociation.'
Agreement on pathway characterization (C76). Both evaluations accept the gradient-based characterization of pathways as part of convergent evidence.
Agreement on pathway integration claims (C77-C78). Both evaluations support findings about pathway interaction and integration regions.
Agreement on probe phase activation patterns (C29-C34). Both evaluations accept these univariate fMRI findings as part of the solid evidence base for pathway dissociation.
Agreement on probe phase connectivity (C35-C39). Both evaluations support these intrinsic connectivity findings that complement task-based activation results.
Agreement on decision phase activation (C40-C45). Both evaluations accept these univariate findings showing dissociable decision-making networks.
Agreement on decision phase connectivity (C46-C51). Both evaluations support these intrinsic connectivity patterns that mirror probe-phase findings.
Agreement on pathway analysis (C52-C55). Both evaluations strongly support the critical pathway analysis with highly significant statistics and bidirectional confirmation.
Agreement on individual-level validation (C56-C59). Both evaluations accept the network composition characterization and individual participant validation.

Agreement on structural connectivity (C60-C61). Both evaluations accept the structural connectivity evidence supporting functional pathways, though OpenEval notes the extraordinarily large t-value should be verified.

Partial disagreement on broader contextualization (C83-C86). OpenEval finds these claims well-supported, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about generalizability beyond the specific stimulus categories tested.

Agreement on speculative nature of peripheral/central vision mechanism (C87-C88). OpenEval rates as uncertain noting it requires empirical testing; peer reviewers' generalizability concerns align with this cautious interpretation.

Partial disagreement on angular gyrus interpretation (C89-C94). OpenEval finds interpretation well-supported by citations, while peer reviewers' concerns about stimulus category generalizability temper confidence in these interpretive claims.

Partial overlap on spatial organization interpretation (C95). OpenEval supports this interpretation; peer reviewers do not specifically challenge it but express broader concerns about generalizability.

Agreement on limitations and future directions (C96-C99). OpenEval views these as appropriate acknowledgments; peer reviewers' concerns about generalizability align with and extend these stated limitations.
Agreement on pathway interpretation caveats (C100-C101). OpenEval supports this nuanced interpretation; peer reviewers' concerns about generalizability are consistent with this careful framing.
